name: Mandatory Fun
editorial_article: Released on July 15, 2014, *Mandatory Fun* stands as the fourteenth and final traditional studio album by American parody legend "Weird Al" Yankovic. Arriving three years after his previous record, *Alpocalypse*, the album marked a significant cultural moment by becoming the first comedy album to debut at number one on the Billboard 200 chart—a feat that underscored Yankovic’s enduring relevance after three decades in the industry. The project was self-produced and released via RCA Records, serving as the final fulfillment of Yankovic’s long-standing recording contract, prompting him to pivot toward a strategy of releasing singles and EPs rather than full-length LPs in the years that followed.\n\nThe album represents a masterclass in modern parody and pastiche, featuring a hybrid approach that blends topical song parodies with original compositions written in the style of various legendary artists. Yankovic meticulously crafted parodies of hits by contemporary stars like Pharrell Williams, Robin Thicke, Iggy Azalea, and Lorde, while his original pastiches paid homage to musical icons including the Pixies, Cat Stevens, and the Foo Fighters. By deliberately choosing to write his original pastiches first and his parodies last, Yankovic ensured that his spoofs remained timely and culturally resonant upon release. Notably, the album’s rollout strategy bypassed a traditional lead single in favor of a week-long digital campaign, launching eight distinct music videos that cemented his status as a pioneer in viral video content. *Mandatory Fun* was eventually awarded Best Comedy Album at the 57th Annual Grammy Awards, solidifying its place as a triumphant closing chapter to his career in traditional studio album releases. The album features a roster of guest talent and parody subjects, including the Pixies, whose style influenced the original track "First World Problems," and collaborators like Amanda Palmer who provided backing vocals for that same song. Other notable entities involved in the spirit or creation of the album include Imagine Dragons, who consulted on their parody, and Cat Stevens, whose work informed the sonic landscape of the project's original compositions.
editorial_pitch: A landmark in comedy music, Mandatory Fun became the first comedy album to top the Billboard 200, serving as the definitive final studio album from parody legend "Weird Al" Yankovic.
